posts.title: Clare Goulet, Closer
posts.description: Normal 0 false false false false EN-CA X-NONE X-NONE Delessaria sanguinea First one found little beauties beyond anything she’ll ever imagine: here’s the head of the algal parade in showgirl feathers, pink peacock fanned à la Rio de Janeiro Carnaval washed up in West Cork. March 1807 is dark sleet on a slate beach so how could this not steal the snow: nine soft fronds sashay like synchronized swimmers circling a diamond mica stud like a story, a star, stunner, Aschenputtel turned belle of the ball its virgin painter never went to and still her arrangement astonishes—a single-celled algae that has never seen a flower has never looked like this. Kjipuktuk/Halifax, Nova Scotia poet Clare Goulet’s second full-length poetry title is Closer (Sackville NB: Gaspereau Press, 2026), a lyric that offers a continuation of the detailed study and sculpted language of her debut, Graphis scripta / writing lichen (Kentville NS: Gaspereau Press, 2024) [ see my review of such here ]. Toronto ON/Montreal QC: I don’t know how I missed this chapbook last year by Toronto poet ( and recent 2026 bpNichol Chapbook Award winner, for her above/ground press title ) Lillian Nećakov , her All My Romeos (Montreal QC: Turret House Press, 2025), a small collection of hefty prose poems. Long known for her engagements with “Canadian surrealism”—alongside poets such as Gary Barwin , Alice Burdick and Stuart Ross , among others [ see my 2021 interview with her on her Surrealist Poets Gardening Assoc. (1984-1993) here ], these poems purposefully blur the real and the surreal, the possible and the impossible, offering new ways to defamiliarize the familiar. posts.title: 12 or 20 (second series) questions with Rosemary Sullivan
posts.description: Normal 0 false false false false EN-CA X-NONE X-NONE Rosemary Sullivan [photo credit: Michael Rafelson] is the celebrated author of over fifteen books of biography, memoir, poetry, travelogue, and short fiction. She is best known for her biography Stalin’s Daughter , which was published in 23 countries and won the Biographers International Organization Plutarch Award, as well as a finalist for the PEN/Bograd Weld Award for Biography and the National Books Critics Circle Award. Her book Villa Air-Bel was awarded the Canadian Society for Yad Vashem Award in Holocaust History. Fierce Attachments: A Life with Cats is her 2026 deeply observed portrait of her two beloved cats, and a beautifully illustrated exploration of the feline spirit. The winner of numerous awards during the course of her distinguished careers, she is a professor emeritus at the University of Toronto and has lectured in Canada, the U.S., Europe, India, and Latin America.
